messages:
anya: Heads-up — noticed sustained saturation on gpu-pool-us-west2 for the past 18m, queue depth on inference-router up ~6x. Cross-zone steering started spilling to us-west-1 which is adding 60–120ms cold-starts and extra egress cost.

mike: Ugh. Any single tenant causing this or broad traffic spike?

anya: Broad traffic — multiple customers. Top offending route is /v1/generate for prod tier. Non-prod looks fine.

sara: Can we quickly throttle non-prod or low-priority prompts at the edge? We have admission control but it's pretty coarse.

raj: We have a short-term knob: reduce global concurrent tokens-to-GPU limit and increase request timeout for non-priority routes. Will that help?

anya: Might. But last time we did blunt concurrency reductions we saw degraded QoS for premium customers because routing still sent them to same pool. Need a tiered reservation.

mike: Proposal: implement a small "priority holdback" — reserve 12% of capacity (vram slots) for premium routes. The rest is fair-share. Also enable model-fallback for best-effort routes to redwood-mini-quant to reduce per-request GPU pressure.

sara: :thumbsup: That sounds good. Do we have a quick config patch we can flip?

raj: I can push a temporary admission config. Something like:

```yaml
admission:
  global_concurrency_limit: 12000
  reserve_by_tier:
    premium: 0.12
    standard: 0.00
  fallback_model_for_best_effort: redwood-mini-quant
  spill_policy: prefer_local_then_region
```

mike: Two notes: (1) prefer_local_then_region prevents cross-region unless local exhausted — reduces egress. (2) fallback_model should also be tied to sequence-length threshold to avoid quality drop on long-context requests.

anya: Also we should enable a soft-queue: best-effort requests get queued up to 8s instead of immediate spill; many clients will retry and not use cross-region.

ops-bot: Incident alert: gpu-pool-us-west2 saturation >= 85% for 12m. Auto-scale attempted +1 node, failed to allocate due to AZ capacity.

sara: AZ capacity limit — that explains autoscale failure. So we need admission + fallback, not scaling immediately.

raj: Rolling out the admission patch to canary now for /v1/generate best-effort routes. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy started: admission-config v2.1 -> canary (eng-infra)

mike: Also, can we enable per-customer circuit breakers so a single noisy customer can't hit premium reservation? If noisy, fall back them to mini-quant automatically.

anya: Yes, add per-customer token-bucket + a short penalty window (30s) that flips fallback_model.

raj: Implemented basic token-bucket rule, pushing tests. If it looks good in 10m we'll roll to 30% of traffic.

sara: Important follow-up: add cost telemetry to see cross-region egress delta and model-fallback savings so PMs can evaluate.

mike: I'll sync with finance after the canary. For long-term: pre-warm smaller model replicas in neighboring regions as cheaper fallback and lower cold-starts.

anya: Thanks team. For now: admission + 12% reserve + fallback to redwood-mini-quant + soft-queue. I'll keep thread updated with metrics. (reacted with :rocket:)
